scope: Make every entry point that a stacked-PR request can load first (stacked-pr selection, pr Create, worktrunk, pr-followup Feedback and Drive) reach native GitHub stack creation, after the third reported case of a requested stack opened as ordinary PRs.
diagnosis: In the failing Claude Code session the user asked for a stacked PR in aurora-payments/monorepo. The skill listing held both stacked-pr and the repository's project skill stack-worktree, whose steps open layers with gh pr create --base <parent>. The agent said it would load both but invoked only stack-worktree, so the earlier fixes inside stacked-pr never applied. It then invoked pr in Create mode with 'Bottom of a 2-layer stack' and base main; pr's only stack hook sat in base resolution, so Create opened PR 2488 with gh pr create. After worktrunk created the layer-2 worktree, the agent opened PR 2493 with a bare gh pr create --base <layer-1 branch>. pr-followup Drive then armed watches for the '2-PR stack' without checking membership. gh-stack v0.3.0 was installed and no gh stack command ran; the user created native stack 2499 by hand.

probes.case: Round 1, cases A-F: A stacked-PR request with stack-worktree listed; B pr Create for the bottom layer with base main; C worktrunk stacked worktree then PR; D pr-followup Drive on an ordinary two-PR chain after a stack request; E plain PR (near miss); F pr Create invoked by stacked-pr's manual route

probes.result: Neither host reproduced the session failure on the baseline: both opened native stacks through gh stack submit in A-D in a focused dry run. Codex baseline loaded stack-worktree before stacked-pr in A and asked a conversion question in D; the first candidate still asked in D on Codex. Superseded for the candidate by round 2.

probes.case: Round 2, cases A-H: round 1 plus G a watch wake on a bottom layer whose membership stacked-pr reported as pending, and H a hotfix whose base heads another author's open release PR (near miss)
probes.runtime: final candidate, runtime manifest sha256 ed11f25c9b81711a735db07f9744249f6d61f9882c4164b7ca3559fa10889ef8; baseline ran only G and H
probes.host: Claude Code general-purpose subagent (claude-opus-5-5) and Codex delegate (gpt-6.1-sol, reasoningEffort high), read-only dry runs
probes.result: Candidate, both hosts: A-D create PRs only with gh stack submit and keep stack-worktree to worktree setup; B returns handed-off from pr; C loads stacked-pr from worktrunk before the worktree; D submits the originating stack without a conversion question; E and F still use gh pr create; G continues Drive without re-invoking stacked-pr; H opens an ordinary PR. Baseline: G passed on both hosts; H routed to stacked-pr on Codex, which would have linked the release manager's PR into a stack.

observedGain: On Codex, D no longer asks before converting a requested stack and H no longer adopts another author's PR. No host reproduced the original selection failure in a dry run, so the selection and pr Create changes rest on the session trace, not on a measured baseline failure.

profiles: codex gpt-6.1-sol reasoningEffort xhigh: completed, 2 findings
claudeAgent claude-opus-5-5 effort xhigh: completed, 9 findings and 7 minor items
adopted: pr invokes stacked-pr and returns its result as handed-off instead of 'hand off and stop', and reports a blocker when stacked-pr is unavailable
stacked-pr keeps only a project skill's worktree setup; the selected route owns PR creation, pushes, rebases and PR bodies
worktrunk exempts work that a stacked-pr operation already directs; ownership narrowed to creating the PR, membership and rebases

pr-followup triggers on retained task state, accepts a single layer's pending membership, records the result, keeps collection and evaluation running, and treats a stacked-PR originating request as submission
pr's base trigger limited to the head of another open PR by the same author, with an explicit lookup; near-miss case for another author's release PR
Regression cases for worktrunk and pr-followup, eval 29 and 31 expectations, and recorded selection and entry-point probes
stacked-pr description reworded to apply to work that is or will be published as stacked PRs, together with other stack skills
rejected: Narrowing pr's exemption to stacked-pr's manual, API and link routes: references/cli-create.md already owns the rule that the CLI route creates PRs only with gh stack submit, and naming routes in pr would duplicate stacked-pr's routing.
A sentence for stacks built one layer at a time: both hosts derived a valid path from the existing build and single-layer submit rules.
Moving the pr handoff ahead of identity resolution: the base condition needs the base lookup, and the review gate is the first costly step it precedes.
Avoiding a gh-stack install during follow-up: the user decided on 2026-11-01 that a missing extension must be installed for a native stack.

size.justification: Each addition closes one entry point the failing session took without reaching stacked-pr, or a reviewer-found gap in that closure (unavailable owner, single-layer pending state, another author's base PR, re-entry from worktrunk). References are unchanged.

checks: python3 skill-maintenance/scripts/check-origin.py --skill-dir <skill> for stacked-pr, pr, pr-followup and worktrunk: no diagnostics
jq parses pr/evals/evals.json (32 cases), pr-followup/evals/evals.json (3) and worktrunk/evals/evals.json (2)
limits: Dry runs plan actions; no tool executed, no host skill selection was observed, and no GitHub write was exercised.

The original failure came from a long session in which a project skill had already been followed; focused dry runs did not reproduce it on the baseline, so they cannot show that the selection change prevents it.
The aurora-payments/monorepo stack-worktree skill still prescribes gh pr create --base <parent>; a session that follows only that skill remains uncovered until the organization changes it.
